tools.title: Aging in place
tools.summary: Goes through the CDC home fall-prevention checklist for the parts the scan can answer, floor by floor: clear paths, steps, stairs, the night path from bed to bathroom, and grab bars.

tools.title: Amenity census
tools.summary: Finds and counts a community's amenities in its scans (gym equipment, laundry machines, pool, lounge, business centre, mail room, playground) and sets them beside what the listing claims.

tools.title: Area profile
tools.summary: Who lives around a building: population, density, household income, age mix, households, the share renting, rent and home value for its census tract, next to the county.

tools.title: Bathroom clearance
tools.summary: Checks each bathroom for a wheelchair: door, turning space, floor space at the toilet and clear of the door, wall for grab bars, and whether the shower has a step.

tools.title: Camera coverage
tools.summary: Shows what indoor security cameras would see, which doors, windows and entry paths they cover, and the blind spots; proposes camera spots if you have none.

tools.title: City census
tools.summary: Rolls up what has been measured across the city: share of homes a wheelchair can live in by zip code, listed-versus-measured area by property type, smoke alarm coverage by building.

tools.title: Commute fit
tools.summary: Estimated drive time from where your people live to each candidate office: the median, who gets a long commute, and transit nearby.

tools.title: Connectivity
tools.summary: How well a place is connected: home broadband on offer (fiber, cable, how many providers), bus and rail stops within a walk, the nearest bikeway and the traffic on the nearest counted road. Offered speeds, not measured ones.

tools.title: Curb to door
tools.summary: Looks at the way in from outside: parking near the entrance, accessible stalls if the aerial photo shows them, how far it is to the door, and steps at the door.

tools.title: Daycare capacity
tools.summary: How many children this space could be licensed for: indoor room area, outdoor play area, toilets and sinks against the Texas or California rule, with the limiting factor named.

tools.title: Daylight
tools.summary: Windows, glass area, the way each room faces and its hours of direct sun on a chosen day.

tools.title: Derived fields
tools.summary: Proposes the record fields this property lacks, measured from the scan and the aerial photo.

tools.title: Door widths
tools.summary: Measures every doorway and flags the ones too narrow for you or what you are moving.

tools.title: Driveway fit
tools.summary: Estimates the driveway's length and width from the aerial photo, how many cars park on it, and whether a trailer, RV or boat fits off the street.

tools.title: Egress routes
tools.summary: The way out of every room: how far, how narrow, which rooms have one way out, and the hose stretch.

tools.title: Facility audit
tools.summary: Your building in one pass: doors, restrooms, ways out, life-safety equipment seen, occupant load and cleaning cost, ending in a prioritised fix list with rough costs.

tools.title: Ask the facts database
tools.summary: Answers questions across every scanned building that no fixed tool covers, with the SQL shown.

tools.title: Feng shui reading
tools.summary: How a feng shui practitioner would read this home: the front door's direction, the Bagua grid on each floor, the command position for beds and desks, and the usual layout notes. A cultural tradition, not a measured effect.

tools.title: Field audit
tools.summary: Across many scans, which record fields disagree with what the scans measure, ranked, with evidence.

tools.title: Field check
tools.summary: Lists what the scan could not settle and a person on site can, and records what they found: confirmed, contradicted or measured.

tools.title: Fire pre-plan
tools.summary: Writes the pre-incident plan from the scans, the aerial photo and the property record, with a one-page printable sheet.

tools.title: Flood rehearsal
tools.summary: Shows what a flood does inside this house: how deep in each room, which doors and windows go under, and the order rooms flood, with the floor-height error carried through.

tools.title: Floor height
tools.summary: Narrows the floor's height above the ground, the flood result's widest uncertainty, from steps counted and fixes taken at your own front door.

tools.title: Furniture fit
tools.summary: Checks whether a sofa, bed, piano or fridge can be carried from the entrance to a room: each door and turn with its margin, and where it would stick.

tools.title: Garage fit
tools.summary: Checks whether your car, truck, van or trailer fits in a scanned garage: how many side by side, the room to open doors, headroom for a lift or roof box, and room for a bench or charger.

tools.title: Hazard profile
tools.summary: Every hazard map at an address in one place: FEMA flood zone, hurricane evacuation zone, storm surge, Hurricane Harvey's high-water marks nearby, sea level rise, earthquake faults, liquefaction and landslide zones, fire hazard zones, urban heat, traffic noise, and weather alerts, earthquakes and wildfires now.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids
tools.summary: Finds scanned homes across Houston or Los Angeles that suit your pets or kids: apartments that allow your dog's weight or cats, houses with a fenced, flat yard and no pool, near playgrounds, parks or dog parks.

tools.title: Industrial fit
tools.summary: Warehouse check: clear height, dock and drive-in doors, truck court and trailer parking, sprinklers, highway, rail, port and power nearby, and flood zone.

tools.title: Kids fit
tools.summary: Whether a home suits young children: stairs that need gates, the pool path with no barrier, windows a child could fall from, a back yard the kitchen looks onto, and the walk to playgrounds, parks and schools.

tools.title: Smoke alarm census
tools.summary: Checks every bedroom's ceiling photo for a smoke alarm and lists where none was seen, as leads to check.

tools.title: Listing claims
tools.summary: Checks what a listing says against the scan, and lists what it leaves out.

tools.title: Loading docks
tools.summary: Counts dock doors and drive-in doors on each wall from the oblique aerial views and beside the CoStar record.

tools.title: Market comps
tools.summary: Comparable properties from CoStar: asking rent, sale price per ft², class, year built and space for lease, and where this building sits against them.

tools.title: Measure search
tools.summary: Finds homes by what is measured inside them: door widths on the way to the bathroom, turning space, wall lengths, floors, steps. No listing site can search this.

tools.title: Nearby
tools.summary: Parks, playgrounds, schools, sports courts and fields, vets, shops and transit near a home, with the walk or ride to the nearest of each along the streets.

tools.title: Noise level
tools.summary: How loud each room is, from the phone's microphone: an uncalibrated A-weighted level per room, best read as which rooms are quieter.

tools.title: Office fit
tools.summary: Whether your team fits this suite as built: desks, private offices, meeting rooms and kitchen, with the listed size and the last tenant beside it.

tools.title: Parking count
tools.summary: Counts parking stalls and parked cars from the aerial photo and compares them with the record.

tools.title: Path to water
tools.summary: Traces every route a small child could take from each bedroom to the pool and names the missing barrier.

tools.title: Permit history
tools.summary: What was permitted at and near an address, by type and year, and any code enforcement cases (Los Angeles); residents' recent service requests to the city nearby in Houston.

tools.title: Pet fit
tools.summary: Whether a home suits your dog, cat or small animal: stairs, floors, a crate and litter spot, a pet door, fall-risk windows, the yard's size, slope, shade and fence, the pool, busy roads, the pet policy and fees, and dog parks and vets nearby.

tools.title: Photo measure
tools.summary: Measures a width or a height from one photo that has a bank card, a sheet of paper or a door of known size in it.

tools.title: Property coverage
tools.summary: For whoever manages or researches a whole property: which of its floor plans and shared spaces have a scan, and which none covers.

tools.title: Earthquake readiness
tools.summary: A safe spot in each room away from windows, tall or heavy furniture near the beds, and where to find the gas shutoff on site.

tools.title: Quiet rooms
tools.summary: Ranks the bedrooms and office from quietest to loudest against road, rail and aircraft noise, from the national noise map, the nearest roads and which way each room faces.

tools.title: Record versus reality
tools.summary: Sets each fact in the CoStar or listing record beside what the scan and the aerial photo measure, with the evidence.

tools.title: What if: renovate
tools.summary: What it would take to make this home wheelchair-ready: the edits, what each one fixes and what it costs, with the renovated plan to compare side by side.

tools.title: Retail site
tools.summary: Parking counted from the air and its ratio, the road the site faces, anchors and neighbouring shops, and walk-in proxies.

tools.title: Risk sheet
tools.summary: One printable page for an underwriter: roof, flood position, wildfire space, pool, trees and interior hazards, each with its evidence and confidence.

tools.title: Robot fit
tools.summary: Shows which rooms a robot of a given width, turning circle and step height can reach and turn in, across one home or many, and which single change to the robot gains the most.

tools.title: Roof facts
tools.summary: Roof material, shape, condition, defects, solar, rooftop objects, trees over the roof and height, read from the aerial photo.

tools.title: Room census
tools.summary: Which rooms this space has, how big each kind is, and which rooms have no type.

tools.title: Room labeller
tools.summary: Names every room of a commercial space from its panoramas, shows what decided each call, and learns from your corrections.

tools.title: Room sizes
tools.summary: Every room's floor area, width, depth and ceiling height, biggest first.

tools.title: Similar rooms
tools.summary: Finds rooms by what they look like ('a sunlit kitchen with an island'), with measured filters: over 12 m², in Houston, room for a wheelchair to turn.

tools.title: Site scorecard
tools.summary: Ranks candidate buildings against your requirements and weights, with a score per criterion, the deal-breakers and the evidence for each cell.

tools.title: Size-up quiz
tools.summary: Training: read a house from outside (bedrooms, stairs, kitchen side, floors) and get graded against its measured interior.

tools.title: Slope check
tools.summary: Uses the phone as a level: a ramp's slope and cross slope against the ADA limits, a threshold's bevel, or how far a door frame is out of plumb.

tools.title: Smoke clock
tools.summary: Minutes of survivable air in each bedroom with its door open and closed, from NIST's fire model run on the measured rooms.

tools.title: Solar roof
tools.summary: Usable roof for solar after setbacks and shade, how many panels, kW, kWh a year and payback.

tools.title: Stairs
tools.summary: Counts the floors, estimates the steps between the entrance and the bedrooms, and finds steps at doorways, floor by floor.

tools.title: Step-free route
tools.summary: Draws the route from the entrance to each room you need, with every door's width, the narrowest point and any step, and says whether you can get there.

tools.title: Storage space
tools.summary: Totals closet and storage area and its share of the unit, and finds bedrooms without a closet room.

tools.title: Storm plan
tools.summary: An ordered plan for the hours before the storm: what to carry up first, where it goes, plywood cut from your real window sizes, sandbags per door, which shutoffs to turn off, and where a generator can safely stand. It changes when the storm or the household changes.

tools.title: Stretcher route
tools.summary: Checks whether a flat ambulance stretcher can be carried from the entrance to each bedroom, and where it would have to be tilted.

tools.title: Sun by room
tools.summary: Hours of direct sun in each room on a day and at the solstices and equinoxes, with neighbours and trees in the way, and the best room for plants, a home office and a cool bedroom.

tools.title: Takeoff bid
tools.summary: Quantities for a trade from the scan (floor by finish, paintable wall, glass, doors, fixtures), priced with your own rates: a cleaning bid, an apartment unit turn, or a fit-out estimate.

tools.title: Tour
tools.summary: Answers by showing: a camera tour from the way in to each piece of evidence the other tools found, with one spoken line at each stop. The last step of a fire pre-plan or a wheelchair check of a home.

tools.title: Truck access
tools.summary: Whether a 53 ft trailer can reach and back to the docks: entrance, gate, court depth, turning room, overhead obstructions, arrival directions and a route on the aerial photo.

tools.title: Turning space
tools.summary: Finds the largest clear circle in each room and checks it against the turning circle you need.

tools.title: Unit compare
tools.summary: Ranks several units or suites side by side on measured area, rooms, storage, windows and door widths, with rent per measured square foot.

tools.title: What sits below the water
tools.summary: Finds the belongings, appliances, outlets and utilities in the rooms that flood, how high each sits off the floor, and what the water would cost, as a range.

tools.title: Walk-through
tools.summary: A quick safety census of a home with no scan, from a short video you record walking through it: rooms, smoke alarms, hazards and belongings.

tools.title: Where am I
tools.summary: Finds the scanned building you are standing in from the phone's GPS, or says there is none here.

tools.title: Wi-Fi coverage
tools.summary: Estimates Wi-Fi strength in every room from a router spot, finds dead zones, the best router spot for the bedrooms and office, and where a mesh node helps most.

tools.title: Wildfire defensible space
tools.summary: Vegetation and tree canopy in California's 5, 30 and 100 ft zones round the house, what to clear first, roof material, slope, the nearest fire station and the CAL FIRE hazard zone.

tools.title: Window check
tools.summary: Point the phone out of a window: its compass confirms or corrects which way the room faces and its hours of sun.

tools.title: Zoning check
tools.summary: What the zoning allows on a lot: the zone, its main uses and height or density limits in Los Angeles; in Houston, which has no zoning, the city's lot-size, building-line and historic rules.

personas.title: Wheelchair user
personas.who: Uses a wheelchair and needs every door, route and bathroom to work for them.

personas.title: Wheelchair user looking for a home
personas.who: Uses a wheelchair and is searching many homes for ones they can get into, around and use without changes.

personas.title: Wheelchair van owner
personas.who: Drives a side-entry wheelchair van and needs about 8 ft beside it for the ramp, and a door the van clears.

personas.title: Older adult or family
personas.who: Is choosing a home for an older relative or young children and cares about safe movement.

personas.title: Planning for an older parent
personas.who: Is checking whether a home is safe for an older parent to live in: trips, stairs, the night path to the bathroom, grab bars, and whether paramedics could reach them.

personas.title: Moving large furniture
personas.who: Is moving a sofa, bed, piano or appliance and needs to know it fits through.

personas.title: Car owner checking a garage
personas.who: Wants to know whether their car or truck fits in the garage, with room to open the doors, and how many cars the driveway holds.

personas.title: RV or boat owner
personas.who: Keeps a boat, trailer or motorhome and needs it off the street: driveway length, and whether the garage door is tall enough.

personas.title: Home robot maker
personas.who: Designs a wheeled home robot and wants to know what share of real homes it can get around, and which change to its size helps most.

personas.title: Fire captain
personas.who: Pre-plans a building: entries, egress widths, hazards, standpipes and the route in.

personas.title: Fire training officer
personas.who: Runs size-up drills on real houses and grades crews against the measured interior.

personas.title: Community risk reduction officer
personas.who: Finds homes and units where smoke alarms are missing, and shows what a closed bedroom door buys.

personas.title: Emergency manager or caseworker before a storm
personas.who: Has a storm coming and a household to advise: how deep the water gets inside, what to move first, and what the people there can finish in the hours left.

personas.title: Houston homeowner before a storm
personas.who: Has a hurricane or flood coming and wants to know what water would reach and what to move.

personas.title: LA homeowner after the fires
personas.who: Lives in Los Angeles after the January 2025 fires and wants to know what to clear round the house, whether the roof is fire rated, and how far the fire station is.

personas.title: Los Angeles household preparing for an earthquake
personas.who: Lives in Los Angeles and wants each room's safe spot, nothing tall that can fall on a bed, the ways out, and the gas shutoff found before the shaking starts.

personas.title: Family planning home security
personas.who: Is planning security cameras and wants every door and ground-floor window watched.

personas.title: Parent of a toddler, house with a pool
personas.who: Has a child under five and a backyard pool, and wants to know every way the child could reach the water.

personas.title: Renter checking a listing
personas.who: Is about to rent and wants to know whether the listing matches the place.

personas.title: Renter checking a listing's claims
personas.who: Has a listing open and wants each claim checked, plus what the listing leaves out.

personas.title: Parent with young kids choosing a home
personas.who: Is choosing a home with a toddler or young children: stairs that need gates, a pool path with no barrier, windows a child could fall from, a yard the kitchen looks onto, and a playground, park and elementary school within a short walk.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids

personas.title: Family checking a neighbourhood
personas.who: Is choosing a home and wants every hazard at the address (flood, fire, earthquake, heat, noise) and what the neighbourhood is like.

personas.title: Family with a teenager who plays soccer
personas.who: Has a teenager who plays soccer: fields and a high school within a walk or a bike ride, a park nearby, and safe streets to get there.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids

personas.title: Dog owner choosing a home
personas.who: Is choosing a home for a dog: a fenced, flat yard with shade, no unfenced pool, a pet door to the yard, room for a crate, a dog park and a vet nearby.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids

personas.title: Older dog that cannot do stairs
personas.who: Has an older dog with stiff joints: no stairs to daily rooms, grip underfoot, a flat yard, a short way out the back door, and an emergency vet within a short drive.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids

personas.title: Cat owner in an apartment
personas.who: Rents an apartment with an indoor cat: the community's pet policy and fees, windows and a balcony a cat could fall from, a litter box spot away from the kitchen, and a vet nearby.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids

personas.title: Remote worker
personas.who: Works from home and needs strong Wi-Fi and a quiet room for the office, fast home internet, a quiet street and transit or a bike route for the days out.

personas.title: Light sleeper or night-shift worker
personas.who: Sleeps lightly or by day and is choosing the bedroom furthest from road, rail and aircraft noise.

personas.title: Plant lover or home office worker choosing a room
personas.who: Wants to know which room gets the most sun for plants, which gives daylight without screen glare for a desk, and which bedroom stays cool in summer.

personas.title: Arranging a home by feng shui
personas.who: Wants a home read the way a feng shui practitioner would: the front door's direction, the Bagua sectors, where the bed and desk go, and their own favourable directions.

personas.title: Home gym in the garage
personas.who: Wants a squat rack and room to press overhead in the garage, maybe with one car still parked.

personas.title: Tennis or pickleball player
personas.who: Plays tennis or pickleball and wants courts within a short walk or ride, with a gym and a park close by.

tools.title: Home search for pets and kids

personas.title: Homeowner considering solar
personas.who: Wants to know how much of the roof can carry panels, what they would make in a year and how long they take to pay back.

personas.title: Agent or host staging a home virtually
personas.who: A listing agent or short-stay host who wants to show the rooms furnished: what fits where, how big each room is, and the light.

personas.title: Film or photo location scout
personas.who: Scouts homes and spaces for a shoot: room sizes and ceiling heights, natural light, parking for the trucks, and a step-free way in for carts and gear.

personas.title: Business checking a site
personas.who: Wants to open or move a business and needs to know whether the use is allowed, what was permitted there, who lives around it and how people get there.

personas.title: Office tenant
personas.who: Is choosing office space and wants seats, meeting rooms and how the plan works for a team.

personas.title: Office relocation lead
personas.who: Moves a company's office: commutes for the team, size for the headcount, rent, transit and access.

personas.title: Industrial tenant rep
personas.who: Finds a distribution warehouse for a client: clear height, docks, truck court, highways, rent against comps.

personas.title: Retail site selector
personas.who: Picks a chain's next store: parking, the road it faces, co-tenants, walk-in trade and rent.

personas.title: Facility manager
personas.who: Audits the building the business already occupies: access, ways out, life safety, cleaning and what to fix first.

personas.title: Apartment manager
personas.who: Runs a building and compares units, accessibility and what the listing claims.

personas.title: Daycare operator
personas.who: Looking for a building to license as a child-care centre and needs the capacity inside and out.

personas.title: Commercial cleaning bidder
personas.who: Prices janitorial work from a scan: cleanable area by floor finish, restroom fixtures, glass, hours per visit.

personas.title: Truck dispatcher
personas.who: Sends trucks to a site and needs the approach, the dock and the doors a pallet passes.

personas.title: CoStar researcher
personas.who: Checks and enriches property records: room types, areas, what changed since the record.

personas.title: CoStar research lead
personas.who: Decides which record fields to fix or add across a portfolio, from where records and scans disagree.

personas.title: Commercial property underwriter
personas.who: Prices a warehouse, an office, a shop or an apartment community: roof, flood position, what is on site against the record, and rent and sale price against comps.

personas.title: Insurance underwriter
personas.who: Prices risk on a property: roof, flood exposure, what was built versus what is recorded.

personas.title: Amenity auditor
personas.who: Checks what an apartment community really offers against its listing, unit by unit and amenity by amenity.

asked: Cranley was built forward-deployed. Before and while building it, we asked people and businesses what goes wrong with the inside and outside of their buildings (homes, garages, stores, kitchens, warehouses, offices), then changed the tools to match (or found they already did): one recorded 31-minute phone interview with Jean Ryan, President of Disabled In Action of Metropolitan New York, written answers from 40 people in 15 online communities, and 340 emails to organisations and businesses.
